description: Dollar-quoted string literals ($$...$$) as the body of a procedure or a function. The point of the form is that SINGLE QUOTES inside need no escaping, so a body may hold a quoted message or an OBJECT_CONSTRUCT with quoted keys and values verbatim. Covered for a procedure and a function, for a body carrying single quotes, for a MULTI-LINE body, for a body with IF / ELSEIF / ELSE and a WHILE loop (whose conditions are PARENTHESISED, as a real account requires - the bare spelling is refused at CREATE), and for a TABLE function. Traditional single-quoted bodies still work, which is the regression guard. One shape worth naming: a table UDF's body is COMPILED at CREATE, so the table it reads must already exist - live-verified, without it CREATE fails 'Object ... does not exist or not authorized'. Converted 1:1 from scripting/DollarQuotedTest (now retired); the Java scanned the SHOW PROCEDURES / SHOW FUNCTIONS ResultSet row by row through JDBC, which becomes a RESULT_SCAN over the same SHOW, and the multi-line bodies are written on one line here except where the multi-line shape IS the claim.

steps.sql: CREATE PROCEDURE test_proc(x INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS $$DECLARE result INTEGER; BEGIN SET result = x * 2; RETURN result; END; $$
CREATE FUNCTION add_ten(n INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS $$n + 10$$
CREATE PROCEDURE quote_test() RETURNS VARCHAR AS $$DECLARE msg VARCHAR; BEGIN SET msg = 'This has single quotes'; RETURN msg; END; $$
CREATE FUNCTION double_value(x INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'x * 2'
CREATE FUNCTION get_numbers(max_val INTEGER) RETURNS TABLE(num INTEGER, squared INTEGER) AS $$SELECT n, n*n FROM numbers WHERE n <= max_val$$
